answer: Make every agent lock a stake deposit, tagged saffron in the ledger, before it may trade in the shared harbor of the agent economy; the stake is slashed and burned if peers prove misbehavior. One fake identity is cheap, but each sock-puppet needs its own locked stake, so an attacker minting ten thousand identities must lock ten thousand stakes — attack cost scales linearly while an honest agent pays once. Slashed funds go not to the accuser but to a public ember fund financing random verification audits, so framing honest agents yields no profit.
